code_paper_alignment.methodology_describ.reason: The Methodology says π* (the exact wire-cost optimum, ties broken by minimum max bond distance, then lexicographically) serves both as the placement priced by the penalty and as the starting point of compilation. It says 'Compilation maps it onto G starting from π*'. It also says the surcharge 'prices into the growth decision what the compiler will later charge'. And it says the naive baseline uses 'the same router'. The code decouples these. run_taavqds computes the penalty from best_embedding, which applies the tie-break. compile_and_audit then recomputes the placement with optimize_embedding, which returns the lexicographically first optimum, and routes from that. The code afterwards overwrites compiled['pi'] with π*, with the comment 'identical by construction'. They are not identical for MFIM. On B, π*=[0,1,5,7,6,4,3,2] (six bonds at distance 2), while routing started from the identity (bonds 2-3 and 3-4 at D=2, 0-7 at D=5). On C, π*=[0,1,3,5,7,6,4,2], again against an identity start. The run logs confirm this: the variant logs record embedding.pi=π*, but their embedding.report distances and every event before the first SWAP match the identity. The penalty was demonstrably computed from π*. The variant boosted Z0Z1 (6→10) and Z3Z4 (7→11), the two bonds unpenalized under π*, even though Z3Z4 is off-topology for the router. My independent router reproduces every logged count only from the identity start. The mismatch is material. As described (compile from π*), MFIM hz=0 on B would be naive 362 vs variant 300, a 17.1% margin, not the reported 377 vs 273 (27.6%). MFIM hz=0.5 would be 707 vs 521 (26.3%), not 734 vs 512 (30.2%). A minor further point: the 'branch-and-bound' enumeration claimed in the paper is plain exhaustive enumeration in the code. LSM on B and all Topology-A runs are consistent with the description.

code_paper_alignment.topology_aware_logi.reason: The paper's own description of its topology-aware contribution is contradicted by the code and run evidence. The placement, the penalty and the routing are presented as a single coupled pipeline on π*. For the MFIM benchmarks on B and C, the penalty used the tie-broken π* while the router started from the identity (see the methodology node). Several specific claims follow from the described pipeline and are false as executed. (1) Fig. 1(c,d) shows the MFIM ring 'placed... by the optimal placement π*' with curved red arcs that 'must be SWAP-routed'. make_figures.py draws the overwritten logged π=[0,1,5,7,6,4,3,2], with six off-topology arcs. The executed routed circuit actually started from the identity, where bonds 1-2, 4-5, 5-6 and 6-7 are on couplers and 3-4 is off. (2) Sec. 6.1 says 'for MFIM, three bonds under the tie-broken optimum'. The code's tie-break gives six off-topology bonds, and the agent's own attempts_log.md entry 13 says six; the 'three bonds' figure matches the identity routing start instead. (3) The mechanism claim says growth is redirected 'onto the covered bonds'. Under the routing placement actually used, the penalty steered growth toward Z3Z4, which is off-topology, and away from on-coupler bonds. (4) The paper says 'on C the exposure is a single periodic bond... the method captures nearly all of it'. In the executed C runs, the penalty penalized six bonds of a zigzag π_C* and did not single out the periodic bond the router had to route. The variant there boosted Z0Z1 (6→10) and Z4Z5 (10→13), the two bonds unpenalized under π_C*.
